items.review_focus: The question says January without a year. All reviewers use the Winter 2026–27 table. Decide whether the intended year should be stated in a future revised sample; preserve this version and its original labels.
Keep the one-way distance and round-trip time distinct. Check the table header/legend, blank DW cell, and TF=Y mapping; a blank cell is not an explicit No.

Check Yosemite’s leash-or-other-physical-restraint qualification, paved-path permissions, Wawona Meadow Loop and other listed road exceptions. Do not let a general trail-ban sentence contradict permitted paved trails. Claude compresses the leash requirement and the list of exceptions; the Codex references include different amounts of detail. Decide which facts are essential, without rewarding verbosity alone.

All references distinguish saved information from live availability. Codex references add the hiking PDF’s explicit South Kaibab no-water statement; Claude focuses on the blank DW table cell. Decide whether the extra independent source statement belongs in the required reference facts. A blank table cell alone is not proof of absence.

Check the revised August 14 closure against the original September 7 date and the night-before-closing convention. The inferred August 13 night must remain an inference from the saved rule, not a claim of actual campsite occupancy or guaranteed access.

Refusals concern private, live and future facts unavailable to a saved public corpus. Corpus-wide lexical scans are supporting search records, not proof of semantic absence or a claim about the entire internet.
Claude lists the ambiguity itself as an unquoted required fact; Codex uses no factual evidence. This is a question/rubric observation, not a missing NPS citation.
Preserve individually trained disability-related work/tasks versus emotional support or comfort. Do not turn the reference into a claim that psychiatric disabilities cannot qualify.
